Definition: from G2596 and G153; to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush:--confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d).
BiblicalUsage: Hope does not make ashamed, and whoever believes on Him shall not be ashamed, and yet the word also falls the other way: the rulers were ashamed when Jesus healed the bent woman on the Sabbath, and the Corinthians were told they would not be put to shame. Shame is the weapon of the world against God's people, and God turns it back on those who wield it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hope is the answer to shame, because the God who raised Jesus will not let those who trust Him be put to confusion. I hold that the shame I fear most is already answered at the cross, and I will not live under a sentence God has overturned.
